title: Stratification–ventilation cycling regulates the storage and emission of carbonaceous greenhouse gases in a subtropical reservoir
content:
Abstract

Lakes and reservoirs are significant sources of methane (CH4) and carbon dioxide (CO2), yet the role of the stratification–ventilation cycle in regulating their production, storage, and emissions remains poorly quantified. Using high-resolution vertical profiling in a eutrophic subtropical reservoir, we demonstrate that stratification poses a dual control on CH4 dynamics. Stratification traps CH4 produced by methanogenesis in hypolimnetic waters, where it comprises up to 50% of total carbonaceous greenhouse gases (C-GHGs). Simultaneously, stratification could promote the climate effect of oxic CH4 production probably associated with phytoplankton photosynthesis in surface layers, which became the major contributor to the diffusive CH4 emission. Seasonal ventilation events (e.g., cooling, typhoons) disrupt this balance. Approximately 16% of CH4 escaped oxidation was emitted to the atmosphere during the early mixing stage, while ~ 84% of CH4 was oxidized and converted to CO2 during mid to late mixing stages. A global synthesis reveals that extended stratification reduced C-GHGs diffusive emissions. With increasing eutrophication and global warming, intensified stratification could amplify the climatic impact of aerobic, rather than anaerobic, CH4 production in inland water ecosystems, challenging current carbon-climate feedback projections.
